Man United CEO Omar Berrada says Red Devils did "absolutely everything" in a bid to keep wonderkid JJ Gabriel

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Matt Law | 20 Nov 2026 15:06, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 15:09.
  • Manchester United CEO Omar Berrada has insisted that the club did "absolutely everything" in a bid to prevent JJ Gabriel from leaving.
  • The 16-year-old recently posted a farewell message to Man United ahead of his expected move to Spanish giants Real Madrid.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 20 Nov 2026 15:06, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 15:09.

Manchester United CEO Omar Berrada has insisted that the club did "absolutely everything" in a bid to prevent JJ Gabriel from leaving.

The 16-year-old recently posted a farewell message to Man United ahead of his expected move to Spanish giants Real Madrid.

JJ Gabriel informed Man United in September of his desire to seek pastures new, just one month before he was expected to pen scholarship terms at Old Trafford.

A professional contract was then expected to follow a year later, but JJ Gabriel's representatives informed Man United that the youngster would be looking to leave the club.

Man United have now lost a player regarded to be a generational talent, but Berrada has stated that the club did "absolutely everything" in a bid to keep him.

According to recent reports, "We did everything. Absolutely everything," Berrada told Sky Sports News when asked about JJ Gabriel's departure.

In a recent development, "Let's not forget with JJ, he's a very young boy with a lot of media attention around him. Our primary concern is his well-being.

"Credit to the academy and people that have been here for many years, they helped him in his development. We still think this is the best place for him to continue his career and to grow.

"This club has a very rich history and tradition of developing young players and giving them the opportunity, as we're seeing this season with Shea Lacey.

"Obviously, Kobbie Mainoo has been doing well for us for a few years now - we're not afraid of giving young players opportunities.

"Obviously, him and his family have taken the decision to leave. We can only wish him the best. We want players that want to be here, that feel being at Manchester United is a privilege.".

JJ Gabriel made his senior debut for Man United in their pre-season game against Atletico Madrid during the summer, but he has departed without making a competitive appearance for the Red Devils at first-team level.

The attacker scored 29 goals and registered four assists in 32 appearances for Man United Under-18s, in addition to two goals and two assists in two appearances for Man United Under-21s in Premier League 2.

JJ Gabriel technically still has a deal with Man United's academy until the end of the season, but the teenager has a European passport through both of his parents, so a FIFA loophole could allow him to become a Real Madrid player from January.

Real Madrid have allegedly already mapped out a pathway for JJ Gabriel into their first team in the near future.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Barcelona have Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez on their transfer shortlist ahead of the January window, according to reports.

Martinez is into his fifth season at United after signing from Ajax for £57million in 2022.

The Argentine has made 121 appearances in all competitions for the Red Devils, but is out of contract at the end of the season.

United do have the option to trigger a 12-month extension to Martinez’s contract, but they may have reservations after he rolled out a scathing public critique of the club’s transfer strategy last month.

And now, Mundo Deportivo reports that Barcelona could be waiting in the wings to pounce as they seek to add a centre-back in the January window.

Inter Milan stalwart Alessandro Bastoni and Borussia Dortmund defender Nico Schlotterbeck are also being considered by the Catalalan giants as options to strengthen Hansi Flick’s side.

But Martinez is viewed as the ‘most economical’ alternative, with the Barca keen on his experience and capability to operate on the left side of defence.

The report adds that Martinez would be willing to listen to an offer, although the arrival of Mauricio Pochettino as United’s upcoming manager could complicate Barcelona’s pursuit.

Pochettino will take charge of his first match against Liverpool on Sunday, but former Red Devils defender Gary Neville expects Martinez will be one of several defenders to make way in the coming transfer windows.

Recent findings suggest that ‘If you look through it now I’d say Martinez would go, De Ligt would go, Mazraoui would go, Mount would go, first wave next summer. Rashford if you can, and Zirkzee,’ Neville said on Stick to United.

‘And then the year after you’d be looking at Shaw, Maguire, Dalot, Bruno, that’s your second wave and maybe then you’ve made your mind up on Baleba and Santos.

‘But the earliest Mauricio Pochettino can unravel this squad is two seasons if he does well. It could take three to get this squad unravelled.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Jose Mourinho has once again called Vinicius Junior "an incredible player" following a positive international break for the Real Madrid winger.

Vinicius has struggled for Los Blancos this season, scoring just once and providing three assists in 12 appearances across all competitions.

The 26-year-old also missed Madrid's last four LaLiga matches before the break after receiving a straight red card for a hair pull against Villarreal.

However, during the international break with Brazil, Vinicius scored a brace against Japan before netting a hat-trick against Singapore.

Ahead of Madrid's league meeting with Celta Vigo, Mourinho reiterated his support for Vinicius.

"Starter, off the bench, or in the stands, it doesn't matter," Mourinho said about Vinicius' role in the team.

"It's a strange thing because, a couple of weeks ago, people were talking about Vinicius as if he were the huge problem Real Madrid had, and after scoring goals against Singapore and Japan, we can't stop talking about Vinicius: if he plays, if he doesn't, why he has to play.

"I think it's too much. What I say about Vinicius is what I've stated one, two, three, four, and five weeks ago: he is an incredible player, we love him, we need him, we have always tried to help him, and that's what we will continue to do.

"Here, we don't have players with privileges. We don't have players who have to play by decree. We have a group of people working for the team, for Real Madrid.".

Madrid are second in LaLiga, three points behind early leaders Barcelona, ahead of welcoming 11th-place Celta to the Estadio Bernabeu.

Celta are one of five opponents Mourinho has faced on more than one occasion in LaLiga with a 100% win rate (W2), alongside Athletic Club (W6), Rayo Vallecano (W5), Hercules (W2) and Real Valladolid (W2).

In a recent development, "Celta are much better than the points they have," remarked Mourinho. They are a team that last season beat us here, at the Bernabeu.

"They are playing in Europe, and perhaps playing matches on Thursdays and then in the league is also costing them some points, but this factor does not exist [for this fixture].

"They will surely present themselves as always: organised and ambitious. They concede few goals because, defensively, they are very organised, and they know how to do it and how to press.".

Kylian Mbappe has scored in each of his last seven appearances for Madrid in all competitions (nine goals) and could equal his best scoring run for the club, achieved between September and October 2025 (eight games, 12 goals).

Williot Swedberg has scored more LaLiga goals against Madrid than against any other side (four in five games).

Since the start of 2024-25, he has been involved in five league goals against Madrid (four goals, one assist), the joint-most alongside Raphinha.

MATCH PREDICTION – REAL MADRID WIN.

Madrid have lost just one of their last 24 LaLiga games against Celta (W21 D2), a 2-0 defeat in December 2025, winning 11 of the last 12.

Los Blancos have won their last eight games in all competitions, their best winning run since a 10-game streak between May and September 2022 under Carlo Ancelotti.

However, Madrid lost their last home game against Celta in LaLiga and have only twice lost consecutive home games against them in the competition (L2 in 1943 and in 2006).

Celta have picked up points in six of their last seven away games against teams from the Community of Madrid in LaLiga (W3 D3 L1), but they lost their most recent such match 3-0 against Rayo Vallecano last October.

Celta have conceded 10 goals and kept six clean sheets in LaLiga 2026-27, both their best records after the first 12 games of a season in the competition since 2002-03 (eight goals and seven clean sheets), under Miguel Angel Lotina.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Frank Lampard appears to have endorsed Chelsea’s pursuit of Alex Scott while revealing his ‘love’ for the ‘quality’ Bournemouth and England midfielder.

Scott has established himself as one of the most sought-after central midfielders in English football having joined Bournemouth from Bristol City back in 2023.

With attentions beginning to turn towards the January transfer window, speculation is mounting that the 23-year-old could have his head turned amid strong interest from the Premier League’s elite.

Though he picked up a thigh injury while on international duty with England last month, Scott’s outstanding performance in the Three Lions’ thumping 7-0 win over Croatia did little to quieten rumours of a potential major-money move.

Arsenal, Manchester City and Tottenham have all been credited with an interest in recent weeks and months, but Chelsea reportedly find themselves in pole position to land Scott this winter.

The Blues are actively scouring the market for midfield reinforcements after failing to bring in a replacement for Enzo Fernandez in the summer and are noted to be ‘increasingly confident’ of reaching an agreement for Scott.

Up until this point, Bournemouth have publicly played down speculation that Scott could be on the move, especially midway through the campaign when they risk derailing the side’s encouraging progress under Marco Rose.

However, it’s understood an offer in region of £100million could be enough to convince the Cherries into selling Scott in what would undoubtedly be one of this January’s biggest deals.

One man who knows more than anyone what it takes to thrive in Chelsea’s midfield is Lampard, arguably the club’s greatest ever player, who won 14 trophies across an illustrious 13-year career at Stamford Bridge.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

During a wide-ranging interview on the Rio Ferdinand Presents YouTube channel, Lampard made it clear just how highly he rated Scott when he was asked to name his dream Premier League midfield three on current form.

‘I don’t want to leave anyone out because there are some teams that are doing some stuff… I’m loving what Brighton are doing at the moment but you do come back to the bigger players sometimes, maybe Cole Palmer or Rayan Cherki,’ the Coventry head coach told Ferdinand.

‘I love Alex Scott at Bournemouth, I think he’s quality.

‘He’s injured now for a short period but I think he’s real quality in that modern all-rounder [role], in the double six/eight.’.

Revealing other candidates for his midfield three, Lampard added: ‘I’ve got to put Elliot Anderson in there, in my opinion, for the way he’s playing.

‘I’m trying to think of the attacking options… I think I’d put Anderson and Declan Rice as the two sixes and then I’ll go for an eight/ten.

It has been revealed that ‘I’m trying to think of the eight-ten that’s really being decisive at the minute. Rayan Cherki is doing bits, I love Cole Palmer.’.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Lampard went on to express his admiration for Martin Odegaard, explaining how he had shut down one of his close friends who had been criticising the Arsenal captain.

‘I really like Martin Odegaard. A mate of mine, an Arsenal fan, doesn’t like Odegaard, he gets on my nerves! He’s a good player,’ he went on.

It has been revealed that ‘He [Odegaard] brilliant. I bumped into him with my son as well recently, him and Kai Havertz, I know Kai, at a hotel, my boy was buzzing and they were so lovely with my boy, not that that makes them good players.

‘They were brilliant, the pair of them. And I said to my son, “This boy [Odegaard] is a good player”, because you see all sides of the game, especially when you do my job and you watch him press and what he does for the team.’.

Lampard also praised Odegaard’s midfield partner Rice and questioned the ‘harsh’ criticism the England international has at times received during his career.

‘I do love Declan Rice and I think he’s become a conversation point because when you get to be so good and compete at such a level, people try to pick holes in your game and I think it’s harsh,’ he continued.

‘I think he’s a really good player and it’s just a common thing that comes with the territory.

‘It’s fine and Declan will just shrug it off.’.

Xabi Alonso has provided Chelsea with positive news about Moises Caicedo.

The Blues manager mentioned on Friday afternoon that the Ecuador captain is fit and available for Saturday’s Premier League clash with Leeds at Stamford Bridge.

Caicedo asked to be substituted at half time in his country’s 2-0 win over Bolivia on Tuesday and later noted it was because he did not feel well and had “other commitments with my club”.

How Mauricio Pochettino's culture shock tactics will resurrect Man United: From 'Murderball' training that leaves players throwing up to telling Harry Kane to slim down and why even the smell of the kit must be spot on

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 21:00 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 17 November 2026.
  • When the entertaining but ultimately rather pointless Ralf Rangnick was tasked with holding the fort as manager at Manchester United five years ago, he was asked whether his much-admired style of football – the high-intensity gegenpress aped by disciples such as Jurgen Klopp – could work with a team that had Cristiano Ronaldo, 36, and Edinson Cavani, 34, in it.
  • Rangnick replied that he was certain it could.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By IAN LADYMAN, FOOTBALL EDITOR.

Published: 21:00 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 17 November 2026.

When the entertaining but ultimately rather pointless Ralf Rangnick was tasked with holding the fort as manager at Manchester United five years ago, he was asked whether his much-admired style of football – the high-intensity gegenpress aped by disciples such as Jurgen Klopp – could work with a team that had Cristiano Ronaldo, 36, and Edinson Cavani, 34, in it.

Rangnick replied that he was certain it could. The German was, of course, proved very wrong.

It is this kind of strange, blinkered hubris that we should not expect Mauricio Pochettino to bring with him to Old Trafford.

Industry observers note that heaven knows we have seen enough of that in recent times. Ruben Amorim and his back three. Erik ten Hag and… well maybe one day we will understand what all that was supposed to be about.

In a recent development, but no, this will not be Pochettino. This cannot be Pochettino.

This United squad is not one built for the fresh United manager’s favoured kind of front-foot, hurrying and harrying football. This is not Tottenham Hotspur 2016. It is not Kyle Walker, Toby Alderweireld, Son Heung-min and Harry Kane. It is not physical and youthful and energetic.

Mauricio Pochettino is waving goodbye to the US national team and hello to Man United this week. But he faces a daunting task at Old Trafford.

This United squad is not one built for the new United manager’s favoured kind of front-foot, hurrying and harrying football.

That is why Pochettino’s battle – at least for the remainder of this season – will be about hearts and minds as much as it is about anything revolutionary that he can bring to bear on the training fields of Carrington.

The good news for those hoping for quick improvement is that Pochettino – at least the one who took Spurs to a Champions League final in 2019 and to within a sniff of a Premier League title a few years earlier – is adept at the mental and emotional side of football. It is upon this that, initially at least, he may wish to rely.

Son told me about this when we sat down to look back on his career in England. He was prolific under Pochettino, a scorer of 75 goals in four-and-a-half seasons under the Argentine. But it was not always like that. Once – just like several current players at United – he was disaffected and unhappy.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Mauricio turned me round and it wasn’t about football,’ Son told me. ‘It was about me as a person and how he made he feel.

Sources indicate that ‘I needed help, basically. And he gave me it.

'He did so many good things that I can't even say the words. It was unbelievable.

Wes Brown believes Manchester United should still be aiming for a top-five finish this season after Mauricio Pochettino was appointed head coach.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss has officially taken the reins at Old Trafford after his final two matches with the United States national team.

Pochettino has undoubtedly been thrown in at the deep end, with United winless in their last eight Premier League matches and facing Liverpool in his first game on Sunday.

But former Red Devils defender Brown believes that the Argentine has the quality to inspire a quick turnaround from his new crop of players.

Sources indicate that ‘Poch is very experienced, and he has his own style of play, but it’s all about consistency, he told Metro. ‘Making the players believe they’re good enough and making sure they do it week in, week out.

‘We’ve had no momentum; we’ve played well here and there in games, and when we did we managed to score, but at the same time we’ve been very poor at times and open to teams scoring at will, making loads of mistakes.

‘The confidence isn’t there, but he’ll be coming in and just trying to get consistency through the team.

‘When a new manager comes in, the players really make an effort, that’s just the way it goes, but then it’s up to the manager to keep that going through the season, and whether or not he’ll be able to, we’ll all have to see.’.

Pochettino brings with him extensive experience in the Premier League but also a proven track record of nurturing young talent into the first team.

Sources indicate that ‘I think at the moment, you are looking at Shea Lacey and thinking, “Yeah, he can get a game”. He delivers, he runs, he works hard.

‘But I also think when you’re in a position where you don’t necessarily just bring in the young lads as well. I think that’s a tough gig if I’m being honest, and you can’t just bring them in when the team’s like this.’.

Pochettino will have to endure a frenetic start to life in the United dugout, with a run of eight games in 21 days starting at Anfield on Sunday.

But with plenty of the season still ahead, Brown thinks United should still be aiming high if they can start fast under their eighth permanent boss since Alex Ferguson’s retirement.

‘There’s still a chance of getting into Europe, 100 per cent,’ Brown added, speaking to Metro ahead of the year’s second Counter-Strike Major.

Industry observers note that ‘Even though it’s been very disappointing, even if you look at the table now, the gap is not that significant. It’s maybe 8-9 points from a European place, if that.

A young Liverpool team has been selected to face Linz – the third youngest, according to Opta, that the club have fielded in the Champions League – and Andoni Iraola is being mindful of players such as Virgil van Dijk and Alexis Mac Allister being overburdened ahead of Saturday’s trip to Brentford.

It has been revealed that one novice who certainly deserves his starting spot is Trey Nyoni, the England Under-21 international has impressed in the opportunities he has been given so far this year. Watch out for his calmness on the ball and the efficiency with which he uses it.

He should get more chances in the next 10 days, as it is difficult to see Dominik Szoboszlai being ready at least until the home match against Brighton on Sunday week.

Asked about Liverpool’s youthful team, Iraola stated: “For me Trey [Nyoni], [Lewis] Koumas and Rio [Ngumoha] are young players coming in from the academy but they are first team players.

It has been revealed that “They are first team players because we trust them, and in our situation, where we have some injuries, and we come from playing three days ago. I think they can play well, and I hope they do well.”.

Sources indicate that it is early days for Bradley Barcola but is has been an underwhelming start to his Liverpool career. The winger was a rotational player at Paris St-Germain, as he is for France, so Liverpool spending £120m is a gamble on his raw athletic attributes and the hope that he pieces everything together.

As Dominic King writes in this piece: “Barcola had no control over the price that Richard Hughes, Liverpool’s former sporting director, brokered with Paris St-Germain for his release. But something he can control is public perception and, with no goals or assists so far, opinions are starting to form.”.

Of the five Premier League teams in the Champions League this season, Liverpool have the friendliest league-phase fixtures and they can secure back-to-back wins against Austrian side LASK in this evening’s early kick off.

Having already vanquished one of their pot one opponents by beating Atletico Madrid at Anfield, Andoni Iraola’s team really should be targeting one of the top spots.

They travel to Linz without some key players, though. Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai missed the defeat by Manchester City and remain sidelined, while Hugo Ekitike is a long-term absentee.

There were positive aspects to Liverpool’s performance against City, but they collapsed like a deck of cards after Ryan Gravenberch’s harsh second yellow card.

Tonight’s game is one they should dominate, and it is a presentable opportunity for Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola to kick-start their seasons and respond to the recent criticism of their performances. Iraola hopes to have a stronger squad to choose from at the weekend, when Liverpool face a stringent test at Brentford. This is the second of nine matches in 28 days for Liverpool.

Industry observers note that “You don’t have a lot of time to train,” stated Iraola. “You try to prepare the games now a lot of times just with the videos and the tactics boards, just a little bit outside. You have to prioritise the freshness of the players.

“Especially now we are playing four games in 10 days, it’s keeping all the legs, all the energy in the games.

LASK are at the moment third in the Austrian league, but booked their place in this season’s Champions League proper with a remarkable comeback from 4-0 down on aggregate against Celtic.

They have injury problems of their own to contend with George Bello and Moses Usor limping off in the weekend’s defeat by league leaders Rapid Wien and Ramiz Harakate tearing his anterior cruciate ligament in July.

They do play on a grass pitch at the Raiffeisen Arena though Kasper Schmeichel, the former Celtic goalkeeper who was working as a TV pundit for the game, was critical of the playing surface.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The main difference between the two job titles is often considered level of input or control of decisions beyond tactics and team selection.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino insists that he wants to be involved in "all the main decisions" at Manchester United.

Pochettino has been appointed as "head coach" of Man Utd, a role he held at both Tottenham and Chelsea, rather than be known as the first-team manager.

The main difference between the two job titles is often considered level of input or control of decisions beyond tactics and team selection.

Mikel Arteta has most notably been promoted from head coach to manager during his seven years at Arsenal, and is widely understood to have a say in almost every key aspect of the club's running.

Pochettino is seemingly not asking for such a level of input, but as the January transfer window approached he has made it clear that he wants a greater say on his players in the future.

"I was in all my career a coach, head coach, manager," he told reporters on Friday. "It does not change too much.

"I know as head coach I am the guy who tomorrow will decide the squad for Sunday, pick the 11, make the changes.

"I know in the future I would like to be involved in all the main decisions that affect the squad. At the end of the day, Manchester United is a football club.".

Pochettino kicks off his Man Utd reign at Liverpool on Sunday.

  • Having limped into the international break, Juve currently trail Italy's top six, while their Venetian visitors are stuck inside the drop zone despite finally posting a second win of the season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 20 Nov 2026 15:24, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 15:27.

Set to clash in Serie A's Sunday lunchtime slot, fallen giants Juventus and promoted strugglers Venezia will meet in Turin this weekend.

Having limped into the international break, Juve currently trail Italy's top six, while their Venetian visitors are stuck inside the drop zone despite finally posting a second win of the season.

Though Juventus are on track to reach the Europa League's knockout phase without needing a playoff, domestic results have been below par for several months.

After missing out on Champions League qualification at the bitter end of last season, the Bianconeri sit seventh in Serie A and are lacking the consistency required to mount a title charge.

Remarkably, Juve have gone 10 league games without consecutively recording the same result, and they signed off for the international break with a run of one defeat, one win and one draw.

Having lost 2-0 to Genoa, before beating Napoli by the same scoreline in Turin, Luciano Spalletti's side had to fight back twice to salvage a 2-2 draw with Fiorentina last time out.

Ahead of Thursday's Europa League game and next week's clash with high-flying Como, they must avoid another slip-up when Venezia come to town.

A former coach of Sunday's visitors, Spalletti is under heavy pressure, and he will only be able to celebrate his 600th Serie A match as a manager if Juventus claim maximum points.

History suggests that the hosts should prevail, as Venezia have lost 11 of their 14 top-flight away games against Juve, while drawing the other three.

In fact, the Lagunari's last victory against the Bianconeri anywhere dates back to a home success in April 1962.

This time, they will head to Turin under survival specialist Davide Nicola, who recently replaced promotion-winning boss Giovanni Stroppa.

Though Nicola's newly introduced side impressively upset Napoli in his first match, they subsequently lost three times without scoring, ahead of a big relegation six-pointer against Udinese.

Sending Stadio Penzo into raptures, Kike Perez scored a stunning goal that separated the pair in a tense 2-1 home win for Venezia, lifting them above their hapless visitors and off the foot of the table.

However, the Arancioneroverdi have yet to pick up any points on the road, while Nicola has previously suffered seven straight defeats in his managerial head-to-head with Spalletti.

Juventus form (all competitions):.

Though Juventus still have a long injury list, full-backs Zeki Celik and Andrea Cambiaso have returned to full training and are both in contention to start.

Francisco Conceicao is also back in the fold, but Kenan Yildiz, Khephren Thuram, Pierre Kalulu, Kamil Grabara, Nico Gonzalez and captain Manuel Locatelli are all unavailable.

Set to start up front, Nick Woltemade finally scored his first Serie A goal against Fiorentina; like strike partner Randal Kolo Muani, he has fared better in this season's Europa League.

After posting three goal involvements from his last two matches, Kolo Muani will hope to continue that form this weekend.

Meanwhile, French wing-back Antoine Hainaut and Nigeria striker Akor Adams are Venezia's joint-top scorers with just two league goals, and the Lagunari have Serie A's lowest shot conversion rate (5.4%).

Either Lion Lauerbach or John Yeboah should partner Adams, the visitors' club-record signing.

Fellow forward Andrea Adorante returned from a layoff during the break, but Marin Sverko and Bartol Franjic are still sidelined.

Juventus possible starting lineup:.

Vicario; Celik, Bremer, Lucumi, Cabal; Luiz, Koopmeiners; Kolo Muani, McKennie, Alajbegovic; Woltemade.

Venezia possible starting lineup:.

Stankovic; Halhal, Moreno, Jesus; Hainaut, Perez, Basic, Sohm, Mazzocchi; Yeboah, Adams.

The pressure is all on Juventus, who have consistently frittered away points with weak defending and wayward finishing.

Even so, the hosts should have too much nous and skill for a Venezia side that face an improbable fight for survival.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andriy Shevchenko has demanded an apology from Chelsea winger Mykhailo Mudryk after he blamed Ukraine’s national team for his failed drugs test.

Mudryk, who is on loan at Tottenham Hotspur from Chelsea, was suspended from November 2024 to July 2026 after he tested positive for the banned substance meldonium.

The 25-year-old initially faced a four-year ban but returned to football this summer after he accepted that he had breached anti-doping rules and agreed to a suspension equal to the time he had already served.

Speaking to YouTube channel Guest of Gordon this week, Mudryk was asked who he felt was to blame for the adverse finding.

‘The environment, the situation in the Ukrainian national team,’ Mudryk said.

‘It should never have existed. I probably haven’t stated it publicly yet but I’m saying it now.

In a recent development, ‘I had never heard of a drug like meldonium. It is a drug you can only get in Eastern Europe. It could only have got into my body in Ukraine. There is no such drug in England.’.

Asked how meldonium got into his system, Mudryuk noted: ‘The Ukrainian national team has absolutely no security system. At clubs, when you travel to an away game, there are always people responsible for what happens on the hotel floors and in the team.

Sources indicate that ‘There are people who keep an eye on it. In the Ukrainian national team we have a nutritionist who hands us pills every couple of days before games. He brings us a little cup. Everyone has to take the pills that are in that cup.’.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Former Chelsea striker Shevchenko, who is now the president of the Ukrainian Association of Football, has hit back at Mudryk’s claims and has described the winger’s version of events as ‘baseless slander’.

‘I want to express my position on the accusations of Mykhailo Mudryk. Loud statements were made about the UAF, the Ukrainian national team. This is a baseless slander against our people, who do their job honestly and professionally,’ Shevchenko mentioned in a statement to Tribuna Ukraine.

‘Instead, after the suspension of Mykhailo Mudryk, his representatives repeatedly approached the UAF with a proposal to artificially find an employee who would take responsibility for the appearance of meldonium in his doping sample.

Recent findings suggest that ‘The UAF refused – such a proposal contradicts the principles of our work. The accusations from Mykhailo’s representatives were not confirmed or proven after many studies and inspections. The investigation and the final settlement agreement with WADA and the English association confirm this.

In a recent development, ‘After Mykhailo became a Chelsea player, the club sent a letter to the UAF requesting that he not be given any medication during the national team training camp. The team staff complied with this request.

‘Head coach Serhiy Rebrov also agreed for Mykhailo to have two of his personal specialists work with him during the training camp. These people monitored his regimen and recovery and helped him with his daily life.

According to recent reports, ‘The UAF has completed all necessary checks in this case. We provided Mudryk’s representatives with the information they requested and have been in contact with those who worked on the case.

It has been revealed that ‘I know people who have been working in the national team for many years. I trust them, because during all this time there have been no incidents in the team that could make one doubt their professionalism.

‘If Mykhailo has evidence to support his words, let him provide it. If there is no such evidence, I expect him to publicly retract his accusations and apologise to the people whose honesty and professionalism he questioned.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Real Betis boss Manuel Pellegrini revealed he "would rather go to the Champions League and not win than win the derbies and finish 15th".

Betis take on rivals Sevilla in LaLiga on Saturday, with both sides looking to make a push for the Champions League places this season.

Betis are fourth after 10 games, seven points behind leaders Barcelona following a 2-0 win over Elche before the international break.

Sevilla, meanwhile, are eight points behind their rivals in sixth ahead of their clash at Estadio Ramon Sanchez Pizjuan.

It has been revealed that pellegrini has won two of his last three LaLiga games against Sevilla (D1), after failing to win any of his previous 10 (D6 L4). Away from home, he has only won three of his 15 matches against Sevilla in the competition (D3 L9).

The former Manchester City boss acknowledged the importance of the rivalry, but has bigger goals in mind for his Betis side.

"I expect Sevilla to have a clear, very direct style of football, they play in their own half and will be a very dangerous team," said Pellegrini.

"The approaches are different every year because the squads are different. Rivalry is always positive as long as it stays on the pitch and not off the field. We will try again to overcome them through our style of play.

"For the fans, winning all the derbies would be important. But if I had to choose, I'd rather go to the Champions League and not win than win the derbies and finish 15th.

"The most notable thing is to get the three points. The best way to win is to maintain the same style of play we highlighted against other opponents. Playing away from home doesn't change our fundamental approach.".

Sevilla have lost two of their last three LaLiga matches against Betis (D1) after not losing any of their previous 12 against them in the competition (W7 D5).

Betis are unbeaten in their last four away LaLiga matches (W2 D2), keeping clean sheets in their last two. They have not recorded three consecutive away clean sheets in the competition since October 2022 (W1 D2).

Sevilla have won just one of their last five LaLiga derbies against Andalusian teams (D1 L3). Betis, however, have lost only one of their last 14 derbies in the competition (W6 D7), but that defeat was against Sevilla (1-0 in October 2024).

Manchester United are considering a move for Freiburg striker Igor Matanovic in the January transfer window, according to reports.

Mauricio Pochettino arrived at United this week having replaced Michael Carrick, who was sacked during the international break.

But the Argentine begins his tenure at Old Trafford without a recognised striker as Benjamin Sesko is sidelined until next year due to a shin injury.

United have made funds available to strengthen Pochettino’s squad in January and the club are targeting a new striker.

According to The i Paper, Matanovic is on United’s striker shortlist alongside Folarin Balogun, who Monaco are open to selling in the January transfer window.

The report adds that United are also looking to bolster Pochettino’s defence with Fulham centre-back Calvin Bassey and left-back Antonee Robinson under consideration.

Matanovic, meanwhile, was signed by Freiburg in an €8 million (£6.8m) deal from Eintracht Frankfurt last year.

The Croatia international, who offers a physical presence in attack at 6ft 5in, has scored 23 goals in 64 games for Freiburg so far.

At international level, Matanovic has scored two goals in 17 appearances for Croatia and came off the bench in three games at the World Cup in the summer.

Matanovic, who is now valued at around €30m (£26m), has also been linked with a move to Tottenham.

When asked about his future in September, Matanovic insisted he had not received an approach to leave Freiburg.

‘As for me, I’m at the moment in Freiburg. There has been absolutely no contact with anyone from my side,’ the striker mentioned.

Chelsea have been fined £150,000 as an FA punishment for offensive chanting during last season’s FA Cup game against Charlton was upheld on appeal.

The charges relate to chanting in the 56th minute of January’s 5-1 win at Charlton, which was Liam Rosenior’s first match in charge of the club.

Chelsea admitted the charge but then appealed against the punishment to an independent body, which upheld the initial punishment.

An FA statement on Friday afternoon read: “Chelsea FC has been sanctioned for crowd misconduct in relation to an FA Cup fixture against Charlton Athletic FC.

“It was alleged that around the 56th minute Chelsea FC failed to ensure its spectators and/or supporters (and anyone purporting to be supporters or followers) did not behave in an improper, offensive, abusive or insulting way with either an express or implied reference to religion or belief.

“Chelsea FC admitted the charge and an independent Regulatory Commission imposed an action blueprint, £150,000 fine and warning as to future conduct following a hearing.”.

The statement continued: “The club subsequently appealed against these sanctions. The appeal was dismissed by an independent Appeal Board and the orders of the Regulatory Commission stand.”.

According to recent reports, chelsea confirmed the verdict in a statement of their own on Friday, adding: “We unequivocally condemn this behaviour. Sectarian abuse – chanting that creates division targeted towards a particular religious or political group – and discriminatory language of any kind has no place in our football club.

“Such behaviour only serves to cause hurt to others and does not represent the values we hold as a club. We want to create a safe and inclusive environment for all, and we have a shared responsibility in delivering this.

Recent findings suggest that “Chelsea takes a zero-tolerance approach towards discriminatory behaviour in whatever form it takes. We will always take steps to identify those responsible and take appropriate action where necessary.

“We understand that further incidents risk additional sanctions against the club and are doing everything we can to inform and educate supporters, as well as develop our existing initiatives to prevent, detect and respond to discrimination in future.

“We know Chelsea fans do not want to see any form of discrimination in our game, and we ask for their support in fostering a welcoming environment at Chelsea matches going forward.”.

The Premier League’s newest managers have a lot to lose

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (758 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Farewell then, Michael Carrick and Pierre Sage, who have gone off to the great big Premier League managerial scrapheap in the sky after an international break where only the identity of the next James Bond could rival speculation over Carrick’s eventual replacement in particular.
  • In Mauricio Pochettino and Thomas Frank respectively, Manchester United and Crystal Palace have gone for a pair of managers whose reputations in English football could do with a good start this weekend to avoid the varying levels of doom that have surrounded Old Trafford and Selhurst Park from peaking again.
  • It’s a good thing, then, that despite their contrasting styles, both are known for putting emphasis on energy – not just in how their team plays on the pitch, but in how the culture around the club feels off it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Farewell then, Michael Carrick and Pierre Sage, who have gone off to the great big Premier League managerial scrapheap in the sky after an international break where only the identity of the next James Bond could rival speculation over Carrick’s eventual replacement in particular.

In Mauricio Pochettino and Thomas Frank respectively, Manchester United and Crystal Palace have gone for a pair of managers whose reputations in English football could do with a good start this weekend to avoid the varying levels of doom that have surrounded Old Trafford and Selhurst Park from peaking again.

It’s a good thing, then, that despite their contrasting styles, both are known for putting emphasis on energy – not just in how their team plays on the pitch, but in how the culture around the club feels off it.

It has been revealed that pochettino has made headlines before for his love of lemons (they absorb negative energy, he’ll have you know) and his apparent sixth sense. In his 2017 book Brave Upcoming World, he wrote: ‘What most influences my decisions is my ability to see if the right energy is flowing.’.

What kind of energy he felt flowing through director of football Jason Wilcox is anyone’s guess at this stage, but his emphasis on things like togetherness and the mindset of his players could finally be the key to starting to turn the Suez canal tanker that United have become, on the pitch at least.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

If Pochettino comes across as part high-level manager, part yoga teacher, then Frank has the air of an executive ready to rebuild the culture at an ailing business.

In a recent development, A year off from football was on the cards after he was sacked by Tottenham in February. The Dane turned down Palace during the summer in favour of World Cup punditry and attending the Tour de France, and didn’t sound completely convinced he’d made the right decision to cut that break short.

‘I was a little bit, “When do I want to go back in? Is it now?” Then this opportunity came up,’ he told PalaceTV this week. ‘I was thinking, this is probably too good to turn down. When I’m sitting here, walking around the training ground, it was just, “Okay, you’re back”, which scared me a little bit, but it’s good.’ Consider the troops rallied.

Questions surround the suitability of both appointments, as Pochettino’s biggest success at Spurs was built on the back of a young, mobile team with something to prove and Frank’s at Brentford came as part of a well-oiled machine. You’d be waiting a long time for anyone to describe United or Palace as either of those these days.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

There’s hope to be found too, for those willing to look for it. Frank did only really have half a bad season and the perceived wisdom is that his personality will suit a ‘smaller’ club – as long as he stays away from any Brighton-branded coffee cups – while of all the managers tasked with fixing United, Pochettino does have the air of a man who can become a messianic figure.

Managerial reputations can only survive a certain number of kicks before there’s no coming back and there may not be many chances left for either man at this level if things go pear-shaped.

However, with both teams playing pretty much every three days for the next month, there are plenty of opportunities for their new managers to shift the vibes back towards a positive setting.

And even if the wins don’t start flowing, transfer enthusiasts should have something to cling on to as Palace and United are reportedly ready to back their newly introduced men with some signings once the January window opens.

It’s nice to have something to look forward to after Christmas, at least.

FC Twente vs Willem II - prediction, team news, lineups

  • Two teams at opposite ends of the Eredivisie table meet on Sunday as FC Twente welcome Willem II to De Grolsch Veste.
  • The hosts are aiming for a fourth consecutive win in this fixture to remain within touching distance of their title rivals, while the visitors are desperate for a victory to spark what has been an underwhelming campaign so far.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adepoju Marvellous | 20 Nov 2026 15:36, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 19:58.

Two teams at opposite ends of the Eredivisie table meet on Sunday as FC Twente welcome Willem II to De Grolsch Veste.

The hosts are aiming for a fourth consecutive win in this fixture to remain within touching distance of their title rivals, while the visitors are desperate for a victory to spark what has been an underwhelming campaign so far.

Twente’s 2-2 draw against Ajax just before the break saw their four-game winning run come to an end, but given they were 2-0 down midway through the second half, securing a share of the spoils resoundingly feels like a point earned rather than two lost.

It has been revealed that just two points behind current leaders PSV Eindhoven, John van den Brom’s side remain firmly in the title race. While they trail Feyenoord, PSV, and Ajax in goals scored, they boast the league's best defence with just 12 goals conceded, and only Heerenveen have kept more clean sheets.

According to recent reports, three weeks after recording their largest-ever win - a 9-0 thrashing of SBV Excelsior - the Tukkers have a chance to lay down another marker against the division’s bottom club. Given rising expectations, a victory here feels almost non-negotiable.

On a personal note, Van den Brom will also want to preserve his impressive record against this weekend’s opposite number; across their previous 11 meetings, the Twente boss has recorded seven wins and four draws.

After winning each of their first home league matches this term, Sunday’s hosts have collected just one point from their last two outings and now seek to avoid going three straight Eredivisie matches in Enschede without a win for the first time since April 2025.

Willem II ended a run of six consecutive league defeats with a 1-1 draw against PEC Zwolle on November 6, but their wait for a first victory continues, as the appointment of Jurgen Streppel has yet to yield the desired turnaround.

Streppel returned for a second spell to replace John Stegeman, who managed just two points from a possible 27 over nine matches. The Zwolle stalemate was only Willem II's third point of the season, at least six fewer than any other team.

Already 12 points worse off than at this stage of their 2024-25 relegation campaign, De Superkruiken face a herculean task to avoid the drop. Upcoming fixtures against Twente and Feyenoord - two of the current top four - over the next three gameweeks only add to their challenge.

A league-high 40 goals conceded means Willem II are frequently punished for their league-low 11 goals scored. Consequently, there must be drastic improvement at one end of the pitch if they are to turn things around.

Facing a team that have scored 14 goals in the final 30 minutes of matches, Sunday’s hosts cannot afford to lose focus in a period in which they have conceded 19 goals, just under half of their season total.

FC Twente form (all competitions):.

Willem II form (all competitions):.

Max Bruns has not featured for Twente since September and remains unavailable, one of two defenders out of contention alongside Stav Lemkin, with the Israeli international suffering a long-term injury just before the start of the season.

Twenty-year-old Filip Erik Thorvaldsen is set to miss a sixth consecutive game for the hosts, who are also still without first-choice goalkeeper Lars Unnerstall.

Wout Weghorst is one of four players tied on nine goals in the Golden Boot race, and the striker will be eager to add to his tally.

Justin Hoogma (knee) and Amine Lachkar (groin) are Willem II’s two guaranteed absentees for Sunday’s clash, with the latter sidelined since July 2025.

However, French shot-stopper Thomas Didillon could also miss out for the away side, having featured just once since mid-August.

FC Twente possible starting lineup:.

Drommel; Van Rooy, Propper, Nijstad, Adelgaard; Zerrouki, Weidmann; Rots, Taha, Orjasaeter; Weghorst.

Willem II possible starting lineup:.

Delanghe; Tjoe-A-On, Dekker, Stam, Ter Avest; Twigt, Zarrouk; Van Crooy, Van Aalst, Vilhena; Haen.

On paper, Sunday’s fixture appears to be Twente’s easiest game of the season so far, but as has been seen on several occasions, things are rarely that straightforward.

Still, we fully expect the hosts to make light work of their visitors and cruise to all three points at the end of 90 minutes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have been dealt a blow in their pursuit of Nico Paz as Real Madrid intend to activate their €80 million (£67m) buyback clause to sign the midfielder from Como, according to reports in Spain.

Paz joined Como from Madrid two years ago and has established himself as the talisman in Cesc Fabregas’ side.

So far this season, the 22-year-old has been one of the standout performers in the Champions League, scoring three goals and registering five assists in four games.

That included a man-of-the-match display in Como’s 4-1 win over United last month while piled more pressure on Michael Carrick.

Last week, reports claimed that United had identified Paz as a potential successor to Bruno Fernandes and were considering a move for the Argentina international next summer.

However, Cadena SER reports that Madrid are ‘determined’ to re-sign Paz at the end of the season and are planning to trigger the €80m (£67m) buyback clause which is part of their agreement with Como.

Madrid had the option to re-sign Paz this year but the midfielder personally requested to stay at Como for another season.

According to recent reports, ‘I thought this was where I would grow the most. I think I made the right decision and I’m happy I did,’ Paz said in September.

Como spent €60m (£51.77m) on their deal to keep Paz at the club but Madrid, crucially, insisted that a buyout clause would remain part of their agreement.

Roberto De Zerbi has said that Mykhailo Mudryk has his full confidence, but must work hard to change the trajectory of his loan spell at Tottenham after a difficult start to life in north London.

Mudryk joined Spurs on a season-long loan from Chelsea on the final day of the summer transfer window, with the club having a £75million option to buy the Ukrainian international at the end of the season.

Mudryk was suspended from competitive football from November 2024 until July 2026 after testing positive for the banned substance meldonium, but it had been hoped he could resurrect his career under De Zerbi.

The pair worked together during Mudryk’s formative years at Shakhtar Donetsk, with the 25-year-old calling De Zerbi his “football father”.

Mudryk, though, has not got going in a Spurs shirt after suffering an ankle ligament injury in training in September.

He had been targeting a return in Spurs’ next two games, but now appears to have suffered a setback after De Zerbi confirmed he would not be available against Ipswich this weekend.

“No, because the proposal was to play Ipswich or Sunderland, or any way to be available,” De Zerbi stated when asked if he would be back to face Ipswich.

“He felt no pain, but not comfortable last week. And they take two weeks more, and step by step we’re going to see the situation.”.

To make matters worse, Mudryk appeared on the Ukrainian podcast ‘Guest of Gordon’ this week and stated that before joining Chelsea in January 2023, he had wanted to join Spurs’ arch-rivals Arsenal before adding that he was using his loan at Spurs to build fitness ahead of a return to Chelsea next summer.

Asked about the comments, De Zerbi said he understood why Spurs fans would be frustrated and asked Mudryk to show his qualities on the pitch.

“Yes, I can understand the fans, but Mudryk is a good guy, he’s a good player,” De Zerbi continued.

“He suffered a lot for the situation in the last couple of years. He has just one thing to do, show on the pitch his qualities, show on the pitch that now he’s playing for Tottenham. Tottenham is a major club, like the other clubs, not less at all.”.

Carles Martinez insisted his Bayer Leverkusen side must be "strong at the back" if they are to defeat Paderborn on Saturday.

Leverkusen have lost two of their last three Bundesliga matches, but defeated Koln 2-1 before the international break.

The Werkself lost 4-2 at home to Stuttgart following a 3-0 defeat at Hoffenheim, leaving Leverkusen fifth in the Bundesliga, five points behind Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund.

Paderborn, meanwhile, are 13th in the league after nine games, three points clear of the relegation playoff places, but also just six points behind Leverkusen.

Paderborn (W1 D3) are one of only three teams, alongside Bayern and Dortmund, to remain unbeaten in their last four Bundesliga matches.

This four-game unbeaten run equals Paderborn's club record in the Bundesliga, previously achieved only in their first four matches in the competition in 2014.

Martinez is wary of the task ahead in Paderborn, but hopes his Leverkusen players will perform in front of their home fans following the international break.

"The changes to the international break schedule are new for everyone," Martinez remarked.

Industry observers note that "We've adapted well. After those gruelling weeks, we've used the time to recover and think carefully about exactly where and how we can improve.

"We can't wait to experience that special [home] atmosphere again – we've really missed it.

"Paderborn are having a good season, have a clear identity and try to dictate the play themselves. That's why we need to be particularly strong at the back. I expect the best from us.".

GTA AND B04 BOTH BACK IN THE SAME WEEK! https://t.co/3D9mcqauMV.

— Bayer 04 Leverkusen (@bayer04_en) November 20, 2026.

Bayer Leverkusen – Patrik Schick.

Patrik Schick has scored eight goals in the Bundesliga this season, finding the net in all four of his home appearances.

Eight goals after nine Bundesliga matchdays equals the club record for Leverkusen, previously achieved only by Schick himself (2021-22) and Patrick Helmes (2008-09).

The Czech forward has now scored as many league goals on his own as the entire Paderborn team.

Santiago Castaneda is the only Paderborn outfield player to have played every minute in the Bundesliga this season.

The American has also recorded the second-most interceptions in the league (25, Kaishu Sano: 27) and has covered the second-most distance (108.4 km, Hennes Behrens: 109.2 km).

MATCH PREDICTION: BAYER LEVERKUSEN WIN.

Leverkusen have not lost any of their seven previous professional meetings with Paderborn in all competitions (W6 D1), winning each of the last six.

Against no other current Bundesliga side have Leverkusen played as many professional matches without suffering a single defeat.

Leverkusen lost 3-2 away to Elversberg on the opening matchday of the Bundesliga season and could now lose consecutive Bundesliga games against promoted sides for the first time since 2017.

However, the Werkself are unbeaten in their last 10 home Bundesliga matches against promoted teams (W7 D3).

Paderborn are one of three teams without an away win in the Bundesliga this season, alongside Koln and Union Berlin.

Paderborn have drawn three of those matches (L1), including two 0-0 draws, and have conceded only five away goals – only Dortmund have conceded fewer on the road (four).

Real Madrid attacker agrees contract until 2031 despite starting just twice under Mourinho

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (812 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 20 Nov 2026 15:39.
  • Real Madrid are reportedly preparing to secure the future of an out-of-favour attacker with an extraordinary £880m release clause, despite his limited involvement under Jose Mourinho this season.
  • Morocco international Brahim Diaz is said to have agreed a latest contract until June 2031, potentially extending his stay at the Santiago Bernabeu by another four years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 20 Nov 2026 15:39.

Real Madrid are reportedly preparing to secure the future of an out-of-favour attacker with an extraordinary £880m release clause, despite his limited involvement under Jose Mourinho this season.

Morocco international Brahim Diaz is said to have agreed a latest contract until June 2031, potentially extending his stay at the Santiago Bernabeu by another four years.

According to Spanish television programme El Chiringuito, the agreement includes a €1bn (£880m) release clause, with an official announcement expected next week.

Journalist Marcos Benito claims the 27-year-old signed the extension approximately two weeks ago, although Madrid have yet to confirm the arrangement publicly.

The reported deal is particularly striking given Brahim's position in Mourinho's squad, where he has struggled to secure regular opportunities despite contributing three assists this season.

His long-term future may be approaching a resolution, but his immediate prospects of becoming a first-team regular appear considerably less certain.

Brahim's existing agreement is due to expire in June 2027, making his future a subject of considerable speculation during the opening months of the campaign.

Real Madrid have been working to retain the versatile attacker, who returned from a three-year loan spell at AC Milan in 2023 and has provided valuable attacking depth in recent seasons.

However, he has found opportunities increasingly difficult to secure since Mourinho took charge.

The former Manchester City youngster has made nine appearances across all competitions in 2026-27, starting only twice and accumulating just 249 minutes of playing time.

His average of fewer than 28 minutes per appearance underlines the limited nature of his involvement, while he has started the last 11 matches on the bench.

Brahim has nevertheless contributed three assists, demonstrating that he can still influence matches during relatively brief appearances.

Competition for attacking positions has become particularly demanding.

Arda Guler has established himself as a more prominent member of Mourinho's plans, while Jude Bellingham and summer signing Yan Diomande occupy crucial roles in Madrid's attacking structure.

Vinicius Junior's anticipated return from suspension and Rodrygo's recovery from injury could further complicate Brahim's attempts to secure additional minutes.

The situation has already prompted questions about his future.

Earlier this month, Sports Mole reported on Brahim's prolonged spell among the substitutes and the growing concerns surrounding his lack of playing time.

Despite those difficulties, Mourinho has reportedly supported the club's efforts to retain the Morocco international.

The proposed extension would strengthen Madrid's contractual position considerably, although a release clause of €1bn should not be interpreted as a realistic valuation or asking price.

Such figures are frequently included in contracts at major Spanish clubs to provide protection against unwanted departures.

There is, however, some uncertainty surrounding the precise duration of Brahim's new deal.

While El Chiringuito reports an agreement until 2031, Spanish newspaper AS has suggested that his renewal is arranged until 2030.

Neither version has been officially confirmed by Real Madrid.

Securing a fresh contract would represent a significant commitment from Madrid, but it would not guarantee Brahim a more substantial role in the team.

His position is particularly intriguing given that the club have several established attacking options and continue to develop younger players competing for similar positions.

For Brahim, the challenge is to turn occasional contributions into a more consistent place in Mourinho's starting XI.

That question also has implications for Morocco, where the midfielder remains an important international despite his restricted opportunities in Spain.

The Atlas Lions are building towards the 2030 World Cup, which Morocco will co-host alongside Spain and Portugal.

National team coach Mohamed Ouahbi has previously expressed a desire to see his players become more influential at club level, while acknowledging Brahim's ability to make a difference for his country.

Former Morocco international Mustapha Hadji has taken a stronger position, publicly questioning whether such limited club involvement is compatible with regular international selection.

Brahim's reported extension therefore raises an obvious sporting dilemma.

Remaining at the Bernabeu offers the prospect of competing for major trophies and retaining his place at one of Europe's most prestigious clubs.

However, the attacking competition that has restricted him to just two starts this season is unlikely to disappear simply because his contractual future is secured.

The deal would also make a potential departure more complicated, with interested clubs likely to require negotiations with Madrid rather than having the opportunity to sign him as a free agent next summer.

There is no indication that Brahim has asked to leave, and his reported decision to extend his contract suggests that he remains committed to fighting for his place.

For Mourinho, the challenge is different: finding sufficient opportunities for a talented squad player whom Madrid appear determined to retain for the long term.

An official announcement could settle the uncertainty surrounding Brahim's contract, but his limited involvement on the pitch remains a separate problem that the newly introduced agreement cannot resolve.

Industry observers note that islands account for a disproportionate share of global biodiversity1, yet insects, including invaluable pollinators such as bees2, remain underrepresented in island biogeography research3. Here we present a global checklist of island bees, recording 4,147 species across 305 islands. Although islands comprise only about 6% of the Earth’s land area, they support around 20% of known global bee diversity, and 42% of insular species are endemic, making up around 8% of all known bee species. Island bee species richness peaks at mid-latitudes (at least in the Northern Hemisphere), mirroring continental trends4. Native richness increases with island area and declines with isolation, consistent with patterns in other taxa5. The strength of island species–area relationships varies among biomes and is steepest in Mediterranean-type systems, which also support disproportionately high bee richness relative to flowering plant diversity. The number of endemic species is highest on large tropical islands, reflecting extensive in situ diversification. Major centres of bee endemism include Madagascar, Malesia (the Greater Sundas and New Guinea) and the Hawaiian islands, where a single large radiation of Hylaeus (Nesoprosopis) dominates6. Among islands that are capable of supporting endemic species, endemism scales strongly with total richness. These findings highlight the need to integrate island bee diversity into global conservation planning and position bees as a model for understanding insect evolution and conservation on islands.

In a recent development, islands are fundamental for studying patterns of biodiversity in time and space1,7. The isolation and limited opportunities for colonization of remote islands have fostered evolutionarily distinct and highly endemic flora and fauna5,8,9. Consequently, islands have long been central to fundamental questions in macroecology, evolution, community ecology and species conservation10. Yet, despite their ecological and evolutionary importance, major gaps remain in our understanding of island colonization, evolution and diversification across animal taxa, especially arthropods.

Sources indicate that insects, the most diverse of all animal groups, remain underrepresented in global biogeographic studies and conservation assessments3. This gap largely reflects logistical and taxonomic challenges of assembling standardized, high-resolution data for insects across geographically and politically fragmented islands, which results in inadequate understanding of species’ distributions11. Consequently, tests of island biogeography theory have disproportionately focused on vertebrates (especially birds) and land vascular plants, and systematic studies across multiple archipelagos remain scarce both for insects and other invertebrates12,13,14 (but see Proios et al.15 for land snails).

It has been revealed that notable global efforts targeting other insect groups do exist, such as the Global Ant Biodiversity Informatics (GABI) database16, as well as efforts motivated by pest and pathogen spread, such as a global checklist of mosquito distributions17, and of patterns of island invasion by beetles18. Comparable progress has been made for Lepidoptera at regional scales, including recent large-scale analyses of butterfly biogeography across tropical Asian islands19. Nevertheless, comprehensive global syntheses—such as those available for plants20—of insect diversity and endemism across island systems are virtually absent.

There are approximately 21,000 described species of bees worldwide21. They have an notable role in global ecosystems, pollinating many wild flowering plants22 and crops23. On continents, bees exhibit a bimodal latitudinal diversity distribution, with peak richness in seasonally xeric mid-latitude regions that support ecosystems with a Mediterranean climate (hereafter referred to as Mediterranean-type ecosystems), as well as in adjacent desert and montane habitats2,4,24. This pattern deviates from the latitudinal diversity gradients of most other groups of plants and animals, which usually peak in the tropics25. Although the continental-scale biogeographical and ecological patterns of bees are becoming better understood, how they translate to island systems remains underexplored.

Sources indicate that generalizations about island bee biogeography have hitherto been rather qualitative in nature. For example, Michener2 noted that whereas very small bees might be carried over long distances by winds, wood-nesting bees may have dispersed across oceans via driftwood: a rafting hypothesis supported by quantitative evidence that wood-nesting bees are overrepresented in island faunas26, Michener also suggested Polynesian transport by seafarers for certain wood-nesting bee taxa that reached some of the most remote oceanic archipelagos, such as the Hawaiian islands. Consequently, bees detected by the even the first European voyages of discovery cannot be assumed to be native.

Recent findings suggest that recent phylogenetic evidence indicates that several bee lineages colonized fresh biogeographic regions during the Neogene Period (around 23–2.6 million years ago) via island-hopping, showing how stepping-stone dispersal may have shaped bee composition. For example, the families Apidae, Megachilidae and Halictidae probably colonized Australia via movements from mainland Asia across the Indomalayan Archipelago27. Similar processes have been proposed to explain disjunct distributions in modern day Central America, where ancient archipelago chains acted as stepping stones between North and South America before the continents joined2.

It has been revealed that conversely, disjunct distribution patterns in other bee groups appear to reflect their more limited capacity to disperse and subsequently colonize islands. For example, following the breakup of Gondwana, stingless bees (Apidae, tribe Meliponini) appear to have been unable to cross the substantial marine barriers that appeared, and their present distribution in Indomalaya probably reflects episodes of sea level fluctuation and transient land-bridges, rather than long-distance overwater dispersal28.

Recent findings suggest that these examples indicate the importance of accurately documenting insular bee diversity to achieve a more complete and fine-grained understanding of global bee biogeography and conservation. Yet, despite this need, comprehensive data remain sparse. Only 542 bee species have been assessed for the global International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) Red List, including just 240 species recorded from islands and 68 island endemics. Of these assessed species, 26 are considered threatened, and for many of these, distributional data are not publicly accessible29. The limited representation of island taxa on global conservation lists does not reflect the well-established vulnerability of island biotas: for example, the majority of US federally listed endangered bee species are native Hawaiian endemics30.

Sources indicate that here we present a global assessment of native bee diversity on islands. Specifically, we investigate: (1) global patterns of native bee richness and endemism; (2) the influence of island characteristics (area and isolation), topography (elevation) and climate variables on both native bee richness and endemism; (3) how endemism scales with richness; and (4) the relationship between insular bee diversity and angiosperm richness. We expect the patterns of insular bee richness and endemism to be shaped by area and isolation, as predicted by island biogeography theory7, but also by biotic and climate constraints and associations, including mutualistic relationships with flowering plants22.

Sources indicate that by addressing these questions, our analyses fill knowledge gaps, providing a global baseline for investigating the evolutionary and biogeographic history, ecology and vulnerability of island bees, while highlighting priority regions for future research and conservation at both archipelago and single-island scales. More broadly, this baseline enables rigorous tests of major hypotheses in island biogeography and (meta)community assembly1 using this taxonomically diverse, and ecologically and economically notable group.

Sources indicate that our final dataset consists of 11,065 unique island-native bee species combinations, representing 4,128 native species across 305 islands (see Methods for details of this classification) (Fig. 1a). Consequently, of the approximately 21,000 bee species described worldwide, our data indicate that 20% occur on islands. Of these, 42% (1,742 species) are restricted exclusively to islands, accounting for around 8% of all described bee species. Although this proportion is lower than that reported for vascular plants, for which 21% of the global flora are island endemic, with 14.5% single-island endemic species (SIEs)9, as well as terrestrial mammals (about 12% single-island endemics31) and rodents specifically (about 17% endemics to islands32), it nevertheless represents a slightly higher contribution of islands to global bee diversity relative to the approximately 5–6% of global landmass represented by islands globally1. Although we focus here on native bee richness, we also recorded introduced species to distinguish genuine native diversity from non-native species accumulation. We identified at least 54 species as introduced on 143 islands, with the western honey bee (Apis mellifera) being by far the most widespread, introduced to 127 islands in our dataset (Extended Data Table 1). Invasion due to anthropogenic drivers is a major threat to insular diversity33, and evidence, at least for A. mellifera, suggests negative effects of invasive bees on native biodiversity on islands (see, for example, ref. 34).

Bee species richness peaks in the Western Palaearctic Realm, whereas endemism (species only found on islands within these realms) is highest on Indomalayan (466 species) and Australasian (443 species) islands (Fig. 1b). Clear differences in island bee richness are also apparent among biomes (Fig. 2), however this pattern is influenced by variation in island area. Species richness was highest in Mediterranean-type biomes: Sicily (approximately 25,000 km2, 636 species), is the island with the highest species richness worldwide and Cyprus (approximately 9,300 km2, 384 species) has the highest species richness of the oceanic islands. The East Aegean islands (approximately 5,000 km2, 589 species) also support large bee faunas, dominated by widespread continental species, reflecting their limited degree of isolation. In contrast to the high richness, endemism on these islands is low, with only Crete (14 species) and Cyprus (23 species) showing comparatively high levels of island endemism. Despite its proximity to the Levant region and its complex origins in tectonic uplift, Cyprus is treated here as an oceanic island owing to its lack of historical land bridge connections to the mainland. The most species-rich Mediterranean-type oceanic island of strictly volcanic origin is Tenerife (2,000 km2, 57 species).

Tropical islands, by contrast, account for moderate overall native species richness compared with Mediterranean-type islands but markedly higher levels of endemism. New Guinea supports 284 species, of which 210 (73%) are endemic, making it by far the richest island in the Australasian realm. The nearby Maluku Islands archipelago (34,000 km2) hosts 102 species, including 62 endemics (61%), and includes Seram (18,000 km2), the most species-rich tropical, oceanic island for bees (87 species).

According to recent reports, in the Neotropics, Hispaniola represents the most species-rich oceanic island, with 66 species. In the Nearctic, the predominantly oceanic California Channel Islands (approximately 910 km2) have a high overall richness (154 species) but low levels of endemism (5%). In the Afrotropics, Madagascar stands out with 226 species, of which 201 (89%) are endemic. Within Oceania, which consists only of oceanic islands, the Hawaiian islands (17,000 km2) are a major hotspot, with all 65 native species of wild bees belonging to a single lineage of Hylaeus (Nesoprosopis), and endemic to the archipelago6. Among other oceanic systems, the Mediterranean-climate Canary Islands (approximately 5,400 km2) host a similarly high number of endemic species (57 out of 128 species), although at a lower proportional level of archipelago endemism (AE) (45%).

Globally, bee richness on islands peaks in the Northern Hemisphere at mid-latitudes (Fig. 1a), mirroring the mid-latitude peak of bee richness observed on mainlands4. This pattern contrasts with the latitudinal diversity gradient seen in other diverse insect groups, such as ants, whose global richness peaks predominantly in the tropics35. The lack of an island-specific bimodal diversity pattern comparable to that found for the mainlands2,4 is probably a consequence of the limited number of Mediterranean-type islands in the Southern Hemisphere. This asymmetry reflects the true distribution of islands globally36, and not simply sampling bias; our global dataset confirms data availability and sufficient coverage across these regions (Fig. 3). This pattern occurs both on continental and oceanic islands, although many of the larger islands within the Mediterranean-type biome were continental or complex in origin. Such environments favour diverse wild bee assemblages through a combination of evolutionary history and ecological conditions. Bees are thought to have originated in the arid environments of Western Gondwana2,27, with limited but predictable rainfall that generates short yet intense blooming periods and a high flowering plant diversity in open habitats2,4,37. These conditions promote temporal synchrony between bee flight periods and floral resources, fostering increased specialization and resource partitioning that reduces competition. This synchrony promotes local speciation and therefore increases richness, allowing these regions to defy the traditional latitudinal diversity gradient2. Our global results support these conclusions but trait-based research focusing on the biome-specific patterns of habitat and dietary specialization of bees on islands are needed to directly test these claims.
